content: On Saturday, November 3, 2012, at 2:30 PM, Dr. Evan Stein will discuss the interim results of the GAUSS study, which evaluates goal achievement after using an anti-PCSK9 antibody in statin-intolerant patients. The study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. The embargo on this information will lift on Monday, November 5, 2012. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Elizabeth A. Magnuson will present findings from the FREEDOM trial, which compares the cost-effectiveness of PCI with drug-eluting stents versus bypass surgery in patients with diabetes and multi-vessel coronary artery disease. The embargo for this data will lift on Sunday, November 4, 2012, at 6:12 PM. At 3:30 PM, Dr. Paul Gurbel and Dr. Magnus Ohman will discuss the TRILOGY ACS Platelet Function Sub-study, which represents the first large-scale platelet function evaluation in an acute coronary syndrome trial. The embargo for this study will lift on Sunday, November 4, 2012. At 4:30 PM, Dr. Timothy Brighton will present the results of the ASPIRE trial, which investigates the use of aspirin for preventing recurrent venous thromboembolism after a first unprovoked event. The embargo for this data will lift on Sunday, November 4, 2012. On Sunday, November 4, 2012, at 1:00 PM, Dr. Bradley A. Bart will discuss the results of the CARRESS-HF study, which is part of the Heart Failure Clinical Research Network. This study focuses on cardiorenal rescue strategies in acute decompensated heart failure. The embargo for this information will lift on Tuesday, November 6, 2012, at 5:13 PM. On Monday, November 5, 2012, at 7:30 AM, Dr. Valentin Fuster will present the main results of the FREEDOM trial, which evaluates optimal management strategies for multivessel disease in patients with diabetes mellitus. The embargo for this data will lift on Sunday, November 4, 2012. At 8:00 AM, Dr. Stephen Wiviott will discuss the TRILOGY ACS Angiographic Cohort, a prospective, randomized trial comparing prasugrel and clopidogrel in patients with non-ST-segment elevation ACS who are medically managed after coronary angiography. At 8:30 AM, Dr. Eric L. Eisenstein will present findings on the economic outcomes of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) performed at sites with and without on-site cardiac surgery. The embargo for this data will lift on Sunday, November 4, 2012. At 10:00 AM, Dr. Jay H. Traverse will discuss the TIME trial, which examines the effect of timing of stem cell delivery following acute myocardial infarction. The embargo for this information will lift on Tuesday, November 6, 2012, at 12:00 PM. At 10:30 AM, Dr. Daniel Sürder and Dr. Roberto Corti will present the results of the Swiss AMI trial, a multicenter study investigating intracoronary stem cell therapy in acute myocardial infarction. The embargo for this data will lift on Tuesday, November 6, 2012. At 11:00 AM, Dr. Renato Lopes will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference in Portuguese. At 1:30 PM, Dr. Massimo Mancone will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference in Italian. At 2:00 PM, Dr. Basil Lewis will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference in Hebrew. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Anne B. Curtis will discuss the BLOCK HF study, which compares biventricular pacing to right ventricular pacing in patients with left ventricular dysfunction and atrioventricular block. The embargo for this data will lift on Tuesday, November 6, 2012, at 4:17 PM. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Roberto Bolli will present interim results from the SCIPIO trial, which evaluates the effect of cardiac stem cells in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy up to two years after therapy. The embargo for this information will lift on Tuesday, November 6, 2012, at 11:30 AM. At 3:30 PM, Dr. Harvey White will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference from a Pacific Rim perspective. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Howard D. Sesso will discuss the Physicians’ Health Study II, a randomized trial investigating the use of multivitamins in the prevention of cardiovascular disease in men. The embargo for this data will lift on Monday, November 5, 2012. At 4:30 PM, Dr. Freek W. A. Verheugt, Dr. Jan Hein Cornel, and Dr. Ton Oude Ophuis will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference from a Dutch perspective. At 5:30 PM, Dr. Lars Wallentin will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference from a Scandinavian perspective. On Tuesday, November 6, 2012, at 8:30 AM, Dr. Paul Armstrong will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference from a Canadian perspective. At 9:00 AM, Dr. Thomas R. Porter will present findings from a prospective evaluation of outcomes with stress perfusion imaging versus stress wall motion imaging during dobutamine or exercise echocardiography. The embargo for this data will lift on Sunday, November 4, 2012. At 9:30 AM, Dr. Gregory G. Schwartz will discuss the effects of the cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor dalcetrapib in patients with recent acute coronary syndrome. The embargo for this data will lift on Monday, November 5, 2012, at 12:00 PM. At 10:00 AM, Dr. Frederick J. Raal will present interim results from the RUTHERFORD trial, which evaluates the reduction of LDL-C with PCSK9 inhibition in patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. The embargo for this data will lift on Monday, November 5, 2012. At 1:00 PM, Dr. Hisao Ogawa will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference in Japanese. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Christoph Varenhorst will provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference from a Scandinavian perspective. At 4:30 PM, Dr. Gilles Montalescot will discuss the ARCTIC study, a randomized trial comparing bedside platelet function monitoring to adjust antiplatelet therapy versus standard care in patients undergoing drug-eluting stent implantation. The embargo for this data will lift on Sunday, November 4, 2012. Dr. Montalescot will also provide a wrap-up of the AHA conference in French.
